articles.summary: Measles outbreak in Tokyo, Japan: 55 cases confirmed this month, bringing the total since January to 109. As of April 5, 71 cases were laboratory-confirmed, with nearly 62 patients aged 10–30 years, comprising about 90% of confirmed cases. This rate is the second-highest since 2008 and may surpass 2011’s annual total of 178. Waning immunity among those vaccinated in early childhood is suspected, while those aged 50+ tend to retain stronger immunity. Japan was declared measles-eliminated by the WHO in 2015; officials attribute the post-COVID rise in cross-border movement to spread. Tokyo Governor Yuriko Koike urged checking vaccination histories in mother-child health records, testing antibody status, and consulting on vaccination; those with suspected infection should avoid going out and seek medical care. Public health measures emphasize vaccination and antibody screening to curb transmission.

articles.summary: Measles is spreading nationwide in Japan, with over 100 confirmed cases in 2026 as of March 24, 2026, prompting spring-break travel warnings. While Yamanashi Prefecture has seen no cases since 2019, the national outbreak continues, with case counts this year approaching half of last year's total. Measles is spread by airborne transmission; early symptoms include cough, high fever, and red eyes, followed by a full-body red rash 3–4 days after onset. There is no specific antiviral treatment; complications can be fatal. Dr. Hiroshi Akaba, pediatrics at Yamanashi University Hospital, notes rising infections worldwide, especially in the United States and Southeast Asia, making travel returnees higher risk. Emphasis on vaccination as the primary preventive measure; due to airborne spread, standard handwashing and masks may be insufficient. If red rash or suspected exposure occurs, consult a healthcare facility by phone before visiting.

articles.headlineTranslated: Explainer: Measles cases have surged 40-fold in three years — How to prevent it? Airborne transmission is also possible at ten times the strength of influenza (Posted March 24, 2026) | YTV NEWS NNN
articles.summary: Measles cases have surged about 40-fold over three years, with airborne transmission driving spread. Measles is highly contagious, about three times more infectious than COVID-19 and more than ten times that of influenza. Symptoms include fever, cough, and runny nose, followed by a rash after fever peaks; immune suppression can raise the risk of complications, with a case fatality rate around 0.1%. The virus propagates via tiny airborne particles, allowing spread in indoor settings. A notable 2016 incident at Kansai International Airport, Japan, involved an imported source and produced a cluster of 33 staff members. To curb transmission, locations used by measles patients have been publicly disclosed to aid containment. The message emphasizes awareness of airborne spread and rapid response to suspected cases to prevent further import/export-linked outbreaks.
